title: Matana
author: Aharon Hyman
attribution: English translation and editorial notes prepared for Joshua Waxman.

paragraphs: In the glosses attributed to ר״ש שלום on Yuchasin, the writer reports having seen in the Megillat Setarim of Mar Nissim Gaon that Rabbi Yochanan had ten sons, all of whom died, and that one son remained to him, named Rav Matana. He was sent to Babylonia to study under Shmuel and was a colleague of Rav Yehuda. Perhaps he is the Rav Matana mentioned without further qualification.[^1]

notes.text: The attribution ר״ש שלום is retained without inventing an expansion of the personal initial. The wording “all of whom died” followed by “one son remained” reproduces the source’s report; no numerical reconciliation is supplied. ושלחו can mean “he sent him” or “they sent him”; the passive “was sent” preserves the event without choosing an unstated sender. Hyman’s attribution to Megillat Setarim and his tentative identification are not independently verified here.
